assessment.nobel_worthiness: Elucidation of GLP-1 as an incretin hormone and its conversion into long-acting agonists has produced one of the most consequential therapeutic advances in metabolic medicine, with proven benefits in type 2 diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular outcomes. The work links basic gut-hormone physiology to large randomized trials, giving unusual clarity and breadth of impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1), Drucker (biology of proglucagon-derived peptides, GLP-2 and therapeutic exploitation) and Mojsov (identification of the active truncated peptide) form a plausible trio. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen was decisive in drug development, but industrial development credit is a separate question; the allocation, including Mojsov versus others not on the list, is contested.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy confirmed independently across multiple agents and large outcome trials; mechanism and safety profile are well characterized. Recognition is timely given the field's current scale.
uncertainties: Priority disputes over who first identified the active GLP-1 peptide are unresolved.
Long-term safety and durability of effect in obesity are still accumulating.
Three-person limit forces exclusion of industrial drug-development contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of the unfolded protein response, a signalling pathway from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus, defined a fundamental principle of cellular quality control with implications for diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer and secretory disease. It is conceptually clean, original and widely taught.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori separately and jointly defined the Ire1/Hac1 pathway and the signalling mechanism; the two-name configuration is natural. Other contributors (for example Kaufman, Ron, Sidrauski) exist, but I am not certain of their precise weighting and they are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is confirmed over three decades in yeast and mammals, including the PERK and ATF6 arms; therapeutic modulation is still maturing, but the basic discovery is mature and stable.
uncertainties: Clinical translation is incomplete, so impact is mainly conceptual.
Credit between the Walter and Mori groups and the mammalian pathway discoverers could be argued.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics turned microbial channelrhodopsins into a tool for causal, cell-type-specific control of excitable cells, transforming circuit neuroscience and enabling vision-restoration trials. Methodological originality and sustained impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: The discovery chain is channelrhodopsin identification and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg), neuronal deployment (Boyden, Deisseroth) and earlier genetic photosensitization (Miesenböck). Credit is crowded and contested; a three-name selection necessarily excludes several decisive contributors, which is a serious fairness concern.
assessment.maturity: Technique is widely replicated and fundamental to neuroscience for over fifteen years; clinical application is only emerging. Recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Allocation among Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg, Boyden, Deisseroth and Miesenböck is unresolved.
This is a tool rather than a discovery about disease or physiology in the strict sense.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells created a new class of living drugs, producing durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and now exploring autoimmune disease. Clinical and conceptual impact is large.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (second-generation CAR design with costimulation), June (clinical translation in CLL and ALL) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early clinical CAR work) is a defensible trio, though Eshhar, Kalos, Brentjens and others contributed and I cannot verify exact priorities.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products with independent confirmation, though long-term toxicity, relapse and solid-tumour limitations remain. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority among early CAR designers (including Eshhar, not on the list) is unresolved.
Efficacy in solid tumours and long-term safety are still limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, the first effective disease-modifying therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, converting a fatal infant neurodegenerative disease into a treatable one. It is a clear example of mechanism-based therapy with striking clinical effect and a platform for other antisense drugs.
assessment.attribution: Krainer identified the splicing mechanism and ISS-N1 target, and Bennett led the antisense chemistry and drug development at Ionis; the pairing is coherent. Contributions from Biogen and clinical investigators, plus earlier SMN1 gene discovery work by others, mean credit boundaries need care.
assessment.maturity: Approval and several years of real-world follow-up confirm benefit; long-term outcomes continue to be defined. Timely.
uncertainties: Industry-originated therapy and the credit boundary with SMN gene discovery are unresolved.
Long-term durability and optimal treatment timing remain under study.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR as the target of rapamycin and the establishment of the TORC1/TORC2 nutrient and growth-control network is a foundational discovery in cell growth regulation, bearing on cancer, metabolism, ageing and immunosuppression.
assessment.attribution: Hall's genetic discovery of TOR is the decisive contribution; Schreiber contributed rapamycin-FKBP12 chemical biology and Sabatini the mammalian mTOR identification, but I treat Hall alone as the cleanest prize configuration with the others' credit left unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed and stable; rapalogs are in clinical use for transplantation and oncology, though broader therapeutic payoff is partial.
uncertainties: A single-laureate configuration may under-credit mammalian mTOR discovery.
I cannot verify the current standing of all individuals on the list and have not weighed non-scientific matters.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 as a regulator of cell survival defined the control of apoptosis in cancer and led to venetoclax, an effective targeted therapy for CLL and other leukemias. The path from basic discovery to a drug is clear.
assessment.attribution: Adams and Cory defined the BCL-2 family at the Walter and Eliza Hall Institute and Vaux showed the survival function; Strasser is also a major contributor to the family. Tsujimoto, Korsmeyer and others made early translocation and mechanism contributions that are not credited here, so this configuration is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed, with an approved drug and a well-understood mechanism. Timely, though Nobel recognition of apoptosis already occurred in 2002.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 apoptosis prize may lower perceived novelty.
Allocation to Vaux versus Strasser or others outside the list is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orexin/hypocretin identified the neuropeptide system whose loss causes narcolepsy type 1, giving a molecular basis for sleep-wake regulation and leading to orexin receptor antagonists for insomnia. It is original and mechanistically clear.
assessment.attribution: Sakurai and Yanagisawa (orexin and its receptors, knockout phenotype) and de Lecea/Kilduff (hypocretin) published concurrently in 1998; Mignot's canine narcolepsy gene work was decisive for linking to disease. Parallel naming and five credited names make allocation difficult.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by human CSF and neuropathology findings and a marketed drug class, though agonist therapies are still in trials.
uncertainties: Simultaneous independent discovery complicates the three-person limit.
Therapeutic payoff for narcolepsy itself is still developing.
